newsitem.title: USA: UPS drivers targeted by Houston police union.
newsitem.headline: UPS drivers targeted by Houston police union.

text.p: A Houston police union urged local officers on Thursday to ticket United Parcel Service drivers for the slightest infractions to show support for the Teamsters strike of the package carrier.

Houston Police Patrolmen's Union President Terry Martin said most replacement drivers operating UPS trucks during the strike lacked commercial drivers' licenses, and pulling them over "would help our Union brothers and sisters at UPS."
"We as union members should go into a 'zero tolerance' mode and do everything possible to get that UPS 'scab' truck off the road," Martin said in a letter faxed to police precincts citywide.

Houston Mayor Bob Lanier assured the Atlanta-based parcel delivery giant that city police officers would not join in the crackdown, and said union members unfairly ticketing UPS drivers would be disciplined.
"We will not tolerate this sort of action," Lanier said.
Martin said a crackdown on the replacement UPS drivers would earn the police union, an AFL-CIO affiliate, support from the Teamsters during future contract talks with the city.
He said the police union also was responding to "citizen complaints" about improperly licensed replacement drivers.
"What we're doing here is a directed type of enforcement to keep the criminal violations off the street," he said.

Negotiators from the Teamsters and UPS were heading to the bargaining table for the first time in four days on Thursday to resume talks on ending a national walkout that has crippled the giant parcel delivery company.
